title: The Essentials — Wii's Signature Library
blurb: The system-sellers. Every one of these helped turn the Wii into the best-selling console of its generation, and most still headline any conversation about the platform's best games.
games: The pack-in game that put a motion controller in tens of millions of living rooms and briefly made bowling a family sport again.
MotionPlus-powered precision turned a simple sequel into one of the clearest showcases of what Wii motion control could actually do.
Nine simple minigames bundled with a second Remote, quietly one of the best-selling games in history almost by accident.
Bikes, a steering-wheel peripheral, and online racing made this the best-selling entry in the entire Mario Kart series.
Gravity-bending planetoid platforming that's still regularly named among the best 3D platformers ever made.
A denser, more inventive sequel that many fans and critics consider an improvement on an already-perfect original.
Adds a story mode, Subspace Emissary, and a much bigger roster to Nintendo's crossover fighter, played competitively for years after release.
The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess
A darker, more mature Zelda launched alongside the console itself, with motion-controlled swordplay built right into the pack-in launch window.
The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword
MotionPlus-driven one-to-one sword combat and a sky-island structure that closes out the Wii's Zelda output on an ambitious note.
Pointer-based aiming brought Samus's first-person adventures to Wii with some of the series' most precise, responsive controls yet.
All three Prime games rebuilt with Wii controls in one collection, widely considered the definitive way to play the series.
A brutally difficult, gorgeously animated revival of the SNES series from the studio that had just finished reinventing Metroid.
Four-player simultaneous co-op turned 2D Mario into a chaotic, screen-clearing party game overnight.
The Balance Board peripheral and daily weigh-ins turned exercise gaming into a genuine cultural phenomenon.

title: Motion-Control Action & Third-Party Standouts
blurb: The games that took the Wii Remote seriously as a combat tool — waggle-powered swordplay, katana-slicing, and a boxing revival that used motion control better than almost anything else on the system.
games: The GameCube classic remapped around Wii Remote aiming, with many longtime fans calling this the best way to play it.
Suda51's beam-katana assassin comedy turned Wii Remote slashing into a stylish, self-aware send-up of open-world game design.
A faster, funnier sequel that trims the original's open-world padding in favor of pure boss-rush momentum.
Black-and-white, blood-red ultraviolence rendered in a comic-book art style, with motion-controlled executions built for maximum spectacle.
MotionPlus sword combat and gunplay in a spaghetti-western-meets-samurai setting, widely regarded as proof the tech could finally deliver.
A loving revival of the NES boxing classic with motion-controlled jabs, dodges, and uppercuts that never feel like a gimmick.
Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure
A pointer-driven puzzle-adventure about turning cursed pirates' enemies into tools, endearing and cruelly clever in equal measure.
A blistering on-rails shooter from cult favorite developer Treasure, praised for some of the tightest bullet-dodging action on the system.
A crossover fighter pairing Capcom characters with classic Tatsunoko anime heroes most Western players had never heard of before.
The PS2 original's sumi-e brush mechanics translated naturally onto Wii's pointer controls, giving the celestial-brush adventure a fitting second home.

title: JRPGs & Long Adventures
blurb: A smaller shelf than other consoles, but a fiercely beloved one — Operation Rainfall's fan campaign to localize this chapter's first three games became gaming folklore in its own right.
games: A sprawling open-world JRPG fought on the backs of two frozen titans, released in Europe in August 2011 — Nintendo of America held off for another eight months, reaching North America only in April 2012 after the fan-driven Operation Rainfall campaign forced its hand.

Hironobu Sakaguchi's real-time tactical RPG reached Europe in February 2012, months ahead of a North American release that didn't arrive until that August — one of the three Operation Rainfall imports fans had to campaign to see localized.

A dark, romance-driven action-RPG about feeding monster flesh to a cursed heroine, published by Nintendo in Europe in April 2012 — North America didn't get it at all until Xseed stepped in a full year later.
Fragile Dreams: Farewell Ruins of the Moon
A quiet, melancholy adventure through a post-apocalyptic Japan where loneliness is as much the antagonist as anything else.
Underwater combat and a fresh set of monsters gave the series a proper Western console debut, complete with a Classic Controller Pro bundle.
Tales of Symphonia: Dawn of the New World
A direct sequel to the GameCube original, following a new protagonist through the world Lloyd and company left behind.
A traditional turn-based JRPG with an idol-pop theme song and a small but devoted following among Wii RPG fans.
A surreal, punishing roguelike remake of a Saturn-era cult classic, as disorienting narratively as it is mechanically.

title: Platformers
blurb: From Nintendo's own yarn-textured reinvention of Kirby to a hand-painted samurai epic and a PC indie darling making its console debut, Wii's platforming shelf ran wonderfully wide.
games: Kirby loses his signature copy ability but gains an entire world made of fabric, yarn, and buttons — one of the most purely charming games on the system.
A return to classic Kirby platforming with copy abilities restored and four-player co-op layered on top — released the same year in Europe under a different title, Kirby's Adventure Wii.
A dimension-flipping hybrid of platforming and RPG systems that swapped turn-based battles for real-time jumping and dashing.
Gorgeous hand-drawn animation and tight platforming marked a full-scale revival for a series that had drifted from its roots.
Hand-painted 2D samurai action across two interwoven stories, one of the most visually striking games the Wii ever received.
A reimagining of the NES classic where feeding a shapeshifting blob different jellybeans solves the game's puzzles.
A wind-manipulation platformer controlled entirely with the Wii Remote pointer, one of WiiWare's earliest and best original games.
Roll a paint-absorbing blob through a monochrome city to restore its color, a colorful, upbeat spin on collect-a-thon platforming.
A remake of the beloved PS1 platformer with redrawn visuals, reintroducing the series' dream-world charm to a new generation.
The beloved PC indie classic's console debut, bringing its Metroidvania exploration and surprisingly deep story to Wii for the first time.

title: Rhythm, Music & Party
blurb: Plastic instruments took over living rooms this generation, and Wii got its own versions of almost all of them, alongside Nintendo's own thoroughly weird music and minigame experiments.
games: A collection of bizarre, deceptively simple rhythm minigames that built a small but fiercely devoted cult following.
The band-simulation phenomenon's Wii port, bringing four-instrument co-op rock stardom to the console a year after launch.
Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock
The Wii port of the series' commercial peak, with wireless guitar peripherals and a setlist stacked with genuine rock classics.
Adds drums and vocals to the guitar formula, turning the series into a full-band experience on Wii.
A turntable peripheral and scratch-based rhythm mechanics gave the genre a genuinely fresh spin after years of guitar-shaped clones.
Hundreds of five-second microgames built entirely around goofy Wii Remote poses, one of the purest expressions of the console's whole philosophy.
A famously divisive experiment in gesture-based musical performance rather than rhythm-accuracy scoring, more toy than game by design.

Motion-controlled minigames layered onto the classic board-game formula — the UK release was pulled from shelves and quietly patched within weeks of launch after one minigame's script used a word that reads as a slur in British English but not American.
A minigame collection built specifically around the Wii Remote and Balance Board rather than retrofitting an existing Mario Party formula.

title: On-Rails & Light-Gun Shooters
blurb: The Wii Remote's pointer made it the best home light-gun controller ever built, and this genre enjoyed a small renaissance here that it hasn't really had since.
games: Retells the events of the first three Resident Evil games as an on-rails shooter, built specifically around Wii pointer aiming.
A follow-up covering Resident Evil 2 and Code: Veronica, with reworked pacing that leans harder into cinematic set pieces.
The House of the Dead: Overkill
A gleefully trashy grindhouse throwback packed with profanity and gore, one of the most purely fun light-gun games on the system.
The House of the Dead 2 & 3 Return
A double-pack remaster of two arcade classics, rebuilt around Wii Zapper aiming for the home light-gun crowd.
An arcade counter-terrorism shooter ported to Wii with Zapper support, prized for its multiple branching mission routes.
A prequel telling the story behind the original Dead Space through on-rails horror-shooter sequences, better regarded than its sales suggested.
A Zelda-themed light-gun game bundled with the Wii Zapper peripheral, built to show off pointer precision more than tell a story.

title: Horror & Mystery
blurb: From a reimagined psychological Silent Hill built specifically for Wii to two courtroom dramas that found an unlikely home here, this chapter shows a quieter, stranger side of the console.
games: A ground-up reimagining rather than a remake, restructuring the original game's story around psychological profiling that changes the game as you play.
A Himalayan mountaineering horror game blending real-world survival tension with vengeful-spirit combat, an overlooked genre entry from an Austrian studio.
Fatal Frame: Mask of the Lunar Eclipse
A camera-as-weapon horror game co-developed with Suda51's studio, released only in Japan on Wii and long sought after by import collectors.
The courtroom-drama visual novel's WiiWare debut, bringing its objection-shouting mystery-solving to a new control scheme.
Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney: Trials and Tribulations
The third mainline Ace Attorney case, arriving on WiiWare with its emotionally heavier storyline intact.
Motion-controlled surgery under time pressure, with two playable surgeons and co-op operations layered onto the series' tense formula.
Expands the surgery formula into six different medical specialties, each with its own distinct motion-control mechanics.

title: Racing & Sports
blurb: Beyond Mario Kart Wii already up top, the console's racing and sports shelf leaned hard into arcade spectacle — off-road demolition derbies, robot-animal races, and snowboarding gone genuinely strange.
games: Launch-window off-road racing with wildly deformable terrain, built to show off what tilt-and-motion steering could feel like.
A stranger, funnier sequel starring robot-animal racers, beloved by the small audience that actually found it.
Arcade soccer with no rules, illegal tackles, and Mega Strikes capable of wiping out a goalkeeper entirely.
A Wii-controlled re-release of the GameCube tennis game, with swing-based motion controls replacing button timing.
Ten arcade sports crammed into one motion-controlled package, a launch-era party-sports favorite despite its scattershot ambitions.
Balance Board-controlled skiing and snowboarding down a mountain that also doubled as social hangout space for up to four players.
A Wii-exclusive entry in EA's snowboarding series, trading some of the series' speed for motion-controlled trick execution.

title: Fitness & Simulation
blurb: The Balance Board and pointer controls turned out to be a natural fit for slower, gentler genres — deep-sea diving, home cooking, and full workout routines that outsold plenty of actual games.
games: An expanded follow-up to Wii Fit adding custom workout routines and new Balance Board minigames.
A structured 30-day workout program using the Wii Remote and Nunchuk as resistance-training feedback, competing directly with Wii Fit.
A calm, violence-free diving sim about exploring the ocean, photographing sea life, and rescuing the occasional shipwreck survivor.
A larger sequel adding a proper story and deeper sea creatures to explore, still built around the original's unhurried pace.
A motion-controlled cooking series entry that turns chopping, stirring, and plating into minigames, disarmingly popular with non-gamers.

title: Puzzle & Strategy
blurb: A smaller shelf than most genres here, but a sharp one — a tactical RPG many still call the series' best, and two very different games about knocking blocks over.
games: A sprawling, difficult tactical RPG spanning multiple armies and perspectives, still cited by longtime fans as a series high point.
A Steven Spielberg-conceived physics-puzzle game about knocking down block towers, deceptively deep beneath its toy-box presentation.
A bigger sequel adding new block types and party modes, refining the original's throw-and-topple physics puzzles.
An indie physics-puzzle darling about building precarious structures out of living, gooey balls, one of WiiWare's clear high points.
A launch-window puzzle-action game about vacuuming up tiny creatures hidden throughout increasingly chaotic, physics-driven rooms.

title: Cult Classics, Curios & Japan-Only Gems
blurb: This is where a 'best of' list earns the word explorer. A Norse mecha-battler, a farming-RPG hybrid, a mosquito-simulator's spiritual cousin in the form of a giant spider — the games that make the Wii library genuinely bottomless.
games: A whimsical kingdom-building game with a surprisingly dark satirical streak underneath its storybook presentation.
A brutal, blood-soaked Norse mythology action game where giants are torn apart limb by limb — one of the darkest things Nintendo ever published, and Japan-only.
A monster-hunting action-RPG with striking hand-drawn art that never made it past Japan on Wii.
A disaster-survival action game bouncing between earthquakes, volcanoes, and hostage rescues, released only in Japan and Europe — never in North America.
A first-person horror game built around the cursed-house film series, using the Wii Remote as an in-game flashlight and phone.

A stealth-horror game about escaping an asylum by brutal means — the BBFC refused it a UK classification outright, and it took a court appeal and a re-edited build before it could legally reach British shelves in October 2008, a full year after its North American release.
An unusual action-adventure told from the perspective of a tarantula and a scorpion, tensely atmospheric and unlike anything else on the system.
A hand-drawn 2D platformer bringing Wario back to his side-scrolling roots with motion-controlled shaking attacks.
A motion-controlled revival of the cartoonish boxing series, punchy and silly in equal measure.
A farming-sim and action-RPG hybrid where tending crops and dungeon-diving carry equal weight.
A Wii-exclusive FPS built to prove the console could handle serious shooter ambitions, with some of the sharpest aiming controls on the system.
A gentle, minimalist platformer from Sonic co-creator Yuji Naka about guiding a flightless bird using stretchy vines.
A tilt-controlled marble-maze game that turned the Wii Remote into a genuinely precise physical controller.
A hyper-stylized musou brawler reimagining Japan's Warring States period as a cast of anime warlords.

title: Licensed Games Done Right
blurb: Closing the collection with the genre most players write off entirely — proof that a licensed spy, superhero, or Star Wars game could still hold its own on this console.
games: LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga
The template for every LEGO game that followed, rebuilding all six Star Wars films as slapstick brick-based co-op.
Applies the LEGO formula to Gotham City, splitting missions between heroes and the villains' own playable side of the story.
A scaled-down but still spectacle-driven take on Starkiller's story, with a distinct Wii-specific build tuned around motion-controlled Force powers.
A ground-up reimagining rather than a straight remake of the N64 classic, with modernized stealth mechanics and Wii pointer aiming that won over longtime fans.
